title: Projection is invertible for the cone of a finite free point-module map
statement: For a commutative condensed ring Λ and any short complex S of point Λ-modules whose first and second objects are isomorphic to finite biproducts of r regular Λ-modules, the scalar-first projection map for the pulled-back mono-cokernel cone is invertible along every scheme morphism and for every unbounded complex K. The comparison identifying the pullback of the cone is exactly modelPull. Exactness of S and any hypothesis on its third object are unnecessary.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions and Formal properties

proof.text: For the projection transformation with fixed $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] says that its functors in the coefficient complex are exact, that it is a morphism of distinguished triangles including the connecting square, and that its component at the unit $O_Y[0]$ is the identity. Finite additivity makes its component at $O_Y^r[0]$ the sum of $r$ identities. Apply it to the cone triangle of $\phi_Y:O_Y^r[0]\to O_Y^r[0]$, whose third object is $P_Y$ by step 3. The first two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its third component an isomorphism. The scalar-first variant is its conjugate by the canonical braidings of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], hence is also invertible. This is precisely the finite-sums-and-cone argument of the unit route; it uses exactness, not commutation of $Rf_*$ with arbitrary colimits.
